opennyai_summary.facts:
The applicants had originally filed criminal revision under Section 397 read with 401 of Cr.P.C.
against the order passed in Criminal Appeal No.60/2018 by the Court of Sessions Judge, Badwani which was a matter pertaining to Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Consequently an application has been filed to convert the present criminal revision into Misc. Appeal.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted a citation of Allahabad High Court in the case of Pradeep Kumar Gupta v/s State of U.P. [Criminal Appeal No.1586 of 2015 decided on 12.05.2015] in which criminal appeal preferred under Section 71 (6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been allowed to be converted into Civil Misc. Appeal and it has been ordered that the appeal be de-registered as criminal appeal and re-registered as Misc. Appeal.
The learned counsel submits that it would be appropriate Court's action to do likewise by this Court as well.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Considered.
It is quite clear that no criminal appeal could have been filed from any order which had arisen out of an order passed under Section 71 (6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and only Misc.
Appeal could have been filed.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
The question is whether this criminal revision can be allowed to be converted into Misc. Appeal.
This criminal revision is allowed to be converted into Miscellaneous Appeal on the civil side and, therefore, it is directed that the instant appeal be de-registered as criminal revision and re-registered as Misc. Appeal.
Learned counsel for the appellant is permitted to make necessary corrections in the memorandum of appeal.
This appeal after re-registration needs to be placed before appropriate Bench as fresh Misc. Appeal in the week beginning 23rd September, 2019.
IA No.7164/2019 stands disposed of in above terms.
